title: When bitterness refuses to leave
issueStatement: The mind keeps returning to hurt, rehearsing offense as if guarding it will protect you.
centralInsight: Forgiveness in Gurbani is not sentimental forgetfulness. It is a disciplined relinquishing of bitterness so fear, pride, and self-protection stop ruling the body.
practicalReflection: The heart becomes harder than the wound when resentment is treated as identity.
actionPrompt: Name the grievance without decorating it. Then ask what holding it is making you become.

source.shortMeaning: Forgiveness, reverence, and fearlessness belong to the same path.
source.lifeApplication: Release can become courage, not passivity.

excerpts.explanation: This keeps forgiveness from being mistaken for weakness.

source.shortMeaning: Soft speech and inward peace are linked to humility and Guru's will.
source.lifeApplication: Forgiveness is easier where posture has already lowered.

excerpts.explanation: Speech, humility, and forgiveness braid together here.

source.shortMeaning: Mercy and reunion are still available where the self expects permanent fracture.
source.lifeApplication: Forgiveness begins more readily when grace is remembered.

excerpts.explanation: Grace keeps forgiveness from becoming self-manufactured moralism.
